Additionally, testing was done at the USU microgrid facility with the OpenADR lab virtual top node (VTN) communicating to the lab virtual end node (VEN), through OCPP to field EVSE devices. Testing has included sending a real-time dynamic energy price from the utility-mimicking controller to the microgrid test site and collecting reports on active power consumption at the site, which are stored in a database for future use and analysis. By September 2025, the OpenADR VTN had been deployed at PacifiCorp in conjunction with the EMS Sandbox DERMS and connectivity between the PacifiCorp VTN was completed with communications verified to control all the DERs at the Microgrid facility. 10 6.1.2 Task 2: Assess Efficiency, Recruitment, And Retention in Participating Buildings PacifiCorp’s UDERMS iCommunity project had six (6) buildings that were participating in the full scope of the project including three multifamily buildings and three commercial facilities. All six of these buildings agreed to participate in the project and had additional intelligent networked EVSE installations completed between October and December 2023. 6.1.2.1 Subtask 2.1.0: Energy Efficiency Assessments and Modelling Six facilities were evaluated for energy savings based on the new construction building design and additional EE improvements that were implemented above and beyond code or standard practice. The six facilities include: 1. Soleil Lofts 2. Citizen’s West 3. Project Open II Building I 4. Utah State University Electric Vehicle Roadway 5. Utah Transit Authority Bus Maintenance Building 6. Packsize The project team obtained building models and building drawings for all six of the facilities to conduct energy assessments of the building model design as compared to local code or standard practice. Building energy modeling work was completed for all six facilities. The modeling and analysis that was performed demonstrated that there are more than 30 percent energy savings for the participating facilities as compared to the baseline. 6.1.2.2 Subtask 2.2.0: Develop Human Subject Test Plan Utah State University developed an initial human subject test plan including the survey deployment and data collection plan. This plan was reviewed by the institution review board (IRB) and received approval in September 2023 (IRB protocol number - IRB: #13568 Connected communities occupant experience survey). The core set of survey questions regarding the occupant experience and consumer comfort was created as part of that package including translation into Spanish that was performed by UC Davis. The survey was programmed in Qualtrics for use and survey deployment. During project team review of the survey instrument, the statistical sampling, the deployment method, and the data collection process, the team made the decision to update the human subject test plan and complete a 11 second submission to the IRB for approval. Input and feedback from the property management company and leadership were also sought and incorporated into the revision. The updated plan was submitted to the IRB and received a second review and approval in February 2024. 6.1.2.3 Subtask 2.3.0: Pre-Deployment Occupant Recruitment and Experience Expectation Significant pre-deployment planning was conducted for the customer experience baseline assessment.
